summary.text: A spring tide is the time, around new and full moon, when the tide's range is at its largest.
It happens because the Sun, Moon and Earth form a line, so the Sun's tidal force adds to the Moon's.
Spring tides bring higher highs, lower lows, shorter slack water and stronger currents than average.

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: From "jump, burst forth, rise", not the season

facts.label: Chart marker
facts.value: MHWS averages high tides on spring-tide days

items.prompt: These big tides come about twice a month, all year round. Where does the name "spring tide" come from?

options.label: They were first recorded in the spring season
The coiled metal springs in old tide gauges
A harbor town where they were first measured
A word meaning to jump or rise, as in a water spring

items.explain: The name is not about the season; it comes from a meaning of jump, burst forth or rise, as in a natural spring.

items.prompt: Tonight is a full moon. What should people at the beach expect from the sea?

options.label: Higher highs and lower lows than average
The smallest rise and fall of the month
Weaker currents than on a normal day

items.explain: Around full moon the Sun's tidal force reinforces the Moon's, so high waters run higher and low waters lower than average.

items.prompt: A kayaker plans to cross a channel with tidal currents. Why might a day around new moon be harder?

options.label: The channel dries out completely at low water
Currents run stronger and slack water is shorter
The tide stops turning for the whole day
Waves are always biggest in the spring season

items.explain: Spring tides, around new and full moon, bring stronger tidal currents and shorter slack water than average.

items.prompt: Spring tides are also called syzygy tides. What does syzygy describe?

options.label: The Sun and Moon 90° apart from Earth's view
The Moon at its closest point to Earth
The Sun, Moon and Earth lined up
The Moon hidden behind the Sun

items.explain: Syzygy is the configuration where the Sun, Moon and Earth form a line, which happens around new and full moon.

items.prompt: A spring tide has just passed. About a week later, what will the tide's range be like?

options.label: Even larger than at the spring tide
Exactly the same as at the spring tide
Gone, with the sea staying level all day
Near its smallest, at a neap tide

items.explain: There is about a seven-day interval between springs and neaps, and at neaps the range is at its minimum.

items.prompt: A tide chart lists MHWS, short for mean high water springs. What does it stand for?

options.label: The average of high tides on spring-tide days
The highest tide that can ever be predicted
The average of low tides on spring-tide days
The average sea level over many years

items.explain: MHWS is the average of the two high tides on the days of spring tides.

paragraphs.heading: The big tides of the month
paragraphs.text: Tides are the regular rise and fall of the sea, driven mainly by the gravity of the Moon and the Sun. The height gap between high and low water over about half a day is called the range. It is not fixed: it grows and shrinks over a two-week cycle. Many shores get two high tides and two low tides each day. A spring tide is the high point of that cycle, when the range is at its largest.

paragraphs.heading: Why spring tides happen
paragraphs.text: About twice a month, near new moon and full moon, the Sun, Moon and Earth form a line. That lined-up position is called a syzygy. The Sun's tidal force then adds to the Moon's instead of working against it. After this alignment, spring tides are sometimes called syzygy tides.

paragraphs.heading: What a spring tide brings
paragraphs.text: During spring tides the high waters climb higher than average and the low waters drop lower. The tides also drive currents that run back and forth, called tidal currents, and these run stronger than usual. The moment such a current stops before turning is called slack water, and at spring tides that pause is shorter than average.

paragraphs.heading: Nothing to do with the season
paragraphs.text: The name has no link to the season of spring. Like the name of that season, it comes from an old sense of jumping, bursting forth or rising. The same idea sits behind the name of a natural spring.

paragraphs.heading: Springs and neaps
paragraphs.text: At first and third quarter moon the Sun and Moon are 90° apart as seen from Earth, and the Sun's force partly cancels the Moon's. The range is then at its smallest, called a neap tide. About seven days pass between a spring tide and a neap. Mean high water springs is the average of the two high tides on spring-tide days, and mean low water springs is the average of the two low tides.
